findings.claim: paginate treats the 1-based page number as a 0-based offset, so page p returns items[p*page_size:(p+1)*page_size] and page 1 is not the first page.
evidence: test_paginate.py:8 asserts only len(...) == 10, so the suite passes despite wrong content (merged from tests-1)
findings.failure_mechanism: caller requests 1-based page 1 -> start = page_size, slice shifted one page forward -> first page of items is never returned and the last page is empty; callers receive wrong data silently

findings.claim: The paginate test asserts only page length and would not fail if page indexing were off by one.
findings.failure_mechanism: off-by-one page offset -> length unchanged for full in-range pages -> test passes while R1 is broken
findings.severity_change_reason: duplicate root cause: a test that cannot fail while R1 is broken is evidence of acceptance-1 and is merged into it (gate step 6); the absent content-asserting test is recorded as a MISSING evidence gap

findings.claim: paginate treats 1-based page numbers as 0-based offsets, so page 1 does not start at index 0.

findings.severity_change_reason: duplicate of acceptance-1 (same defect at paginate.py:2); merged
